text:
Full-stack structure & endpoint reference — React frontend + Express/PostgreSQL backend
This is your single source of truth while building: what folders/files to create, what each backend endpoint does, what each React piece
needs to call, and exactly how the two sides connect (cookies, CORS, env vars). Database schema and API contract match the original
capstone spec — only the frontend is React instead of vanilla JS.

Backend/
├── server.js                 // entry point — imports app, calls app.listen()
├── app.js                    // Express app: middleware, routes mounted here
├── .env                      // already exists — DB creds, JWT secret, PORT
├── db/
│   ├── index.js              // already exists — pg Pool + query()
│   └── InitDb.js              // already exists — CREATE TABLE statements
├── utils/
│   ├── jwt.js                 // already exists — sign/verify/cookie helpers
│   └── password.js            // already exists — bcrypt hash/compare
├── middleware/
│   ├── requireAuth.js          // verifies JWT cookie, sets req.user
│   ├── requireProjectMember.js  // checks project_members row exists
│   └── requireProjectAdmin.js   // same + role === 'admin'
├── controllers/
│   ├── authController.js       // register, login, logout logic
│   ├── projectController.js    // create/list/get project, invite
│   ├── taskController.js       // list/create/update tasks
│   └── activityController.js   // get activity feed
└── routes/
├── authRoutes.js
├── projectRoutes.js
├── taskRoutes.js
└── activityRoutes.js
Controller/Service/Route pattern, simplified for your timeline: routes define the URL + which middleware runs, controllers hold the actual
logic and talk to the DB directly via query() . Skip a separate "service" layer unless you have spare time — for a 1-day build, routes →
controllers → db is enough layering.

All tasks. Supports ?status= , ?priority= , ?assignedTo= , ?search= .
POST
/api/projects/:id/tasks
Project Member
Create task (title, description, priority, due_date). Logs activity.
PUT
/api/tasks/:taskId
Project Member
Update status/assignee/priority/due_date. Logs activity on status or assignee change.
GET
/api/projects/:id/activity
Project Member
Latest 20 activity_logs rows, newest first.
Middleware order matters: requireAuth always runs first (it needs to set req.user before anything else can check membership).
requireProjectMember / requireProjectAdmin run next, and read req.params.id — so your route param must literally be named :id for
that to work without extra code.
